clue.text: Approval and praise within part of theatre

indicators.note: one thing set within another is held inside it, so the praise word sits inside the theatre word

parts.note: the pit is the area in front of the stage, or the stalls

explanation.surface: Applause and acclaim ringing out from one section of the auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or enthusiastic approval, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 2
Copter is a wreck ultimately after struggling in turbulence?

indicators.note: letters struggling are thrashing about out of order
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A helicopter crashed after battling through rough air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' looks like part of the story, but only its last letter joins the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Air pockets are regions of downdraught that jolt aircraft, a cause of turbulence, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Discourage daughter over another relative

explanation.surface: Putting off a girl from visiting another family member.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt is to intimidate or dishearten, which discourages someone.

clue.text: Cross, saying a few words about party that's terminated early

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other
ended before its time, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rave is a dance party

explanation.surface: Someone gives a brief, irritated speech about a party that ended too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, which fits the short speech; it is the verb, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse land is to travel across it, so it means cross as a verb.

clue.text: Carry audio device full of symbolism

explanation.surface: Lugging around a piece of sound equipment that is laden with meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem standing for a clan or spirit, so totemic things are heavily symbolic.

clue.text: Not quite leading city of the past

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: the best means the leading one

explanation.surface: A city that was nearly foremost in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great ancient city in Egypt, and another in Greece, both long past their prime.

clue.text: Landing requires ability with feathers

parts.note: a deft touch is a skill

explanation.surface: A bird coming in to land needs skill with its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchdown is the moment an aircraft lands on the runway.

clue.text: Tailor madly working, without skill

indicators.note: letters working are in motion and get set into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tailor sewing in a frenzy, botching the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' feels like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'working' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or inept, so acting maladroitly is acting without skill.

clue.text: Injury on opponents' ground? Here's simultaneous shot

parts.note: playing away is playing at the opposing team's ground

explanation.surface: A player picks up a wound at an away match, while the camera grabs a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In film, a cutaway is a shot of action elsewhere happening at the same time, interrupting the main scene.

clue.text: Top show cut before delayed broadcast

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the show loses its final letter

parts.note: a circus is held under the big top

explanation.surface: A leading programme is edited before going out on a time-delay transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top show' reads as a hit programme; in fact the Big Top is a circus tent.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news or rumours is to spread them around, which is to circulate them.

clue.text: Piece of equipment containing minimum of light is dark

indicators.note: the equipment word holds the selected letter inside it

parts.note: a unit is a single piece of apparatus

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, a single opening letter

explanation.surface: A gadget that barely lets any light in leaves things in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without lighting switched on is dark, so the two are synonyms here.

clue.text: Arts subject, in brief, to include old Anglo-American poet

indicators.note: the subject word takes in the extra letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Eng Lit, English Literature, shortened further

explanation.surface: A short literature course expanding to cover a veteran transatlantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was born in St Louis and became a British citizen, hence Anglo-American.

clue.text: Scenario with hod redesigned? Probably not this shape

indicators.note: redesigned means made over in a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Imagining a remodelled bricklayer's carrier, which surely would not take a twenty-faced form.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is a builder's open trough on a pole for carrying bricks; 'Probably not' is the joke that no such redesign would end up this shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An icosahedron is a solid with twenty faces, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Certainly experienced expression of pain after last of unsafe cosmetic

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter only

parts.note: had a bad time means experienced one

explanation.surface: Someone yelped in pain after using a dodgy make-up product.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a coloured make-up applied to the eyelids, an example of a cosmetic.

clue.text: Shopkeeper, perhaps, conventional in such things at the outset

parts.note: a stock response is a conventional one

indicators.note: at the outset of each word means take only its opening letter

parts.note: opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A retailer is, perhaps, traditional when it comes to such goods to start with.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockist is a retailer who carries a particular product, so a shopkeeper is one example.

clue.text: A research area in Korea hybridised marsupial

indicators.note: hybridised means crossed and mixed together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: a lab is where research is done

explanation.surface: A Korean laboratory has bred a crossbreed of pouched mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial; the name koala bear is popular though it is not a bear.

clue.text: Uncovered coot record given variable study of eggs

indicators.note: uncovering a word strips its outer letters, leaving the inside

parts.note: coot without its first and last letters
algebra's variables are x, y, z

explanation.surface: An exposed water bird's record is credited with a changeable value.
explanation.walkthrough: A coot is a water bird, apt in a clue about eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oology is the branch of zoology concerned with collecting and studying birds' eggs.

clue.text: Satisfied infantryman took charge

parts.note: grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier

explanation.surface: A foot soldier was content when he commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a jokey back-formation from disgruntled.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruntled is the humorous opposite of disgruntled, meaning pleased or contented.

clue.text: Medicine man mostly reasonable after eating meat

indicators.note: the shortened word swallows the meat, holding it inside
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A healer turns mostly rational once he has had a meal of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spiritual guide, which is what a medicine man is.

clue.text: Bit of water brought in to lightly boil fish?

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the letter enters the cooking word

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a scrap of it, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Adding a splash of water to poach a fish gently.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen reading makes fish the food; the question mark says a fish is defined loosely as one that swims.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is an example of a creature that swims, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hectic rearranged tie hosted by European people — Hearts knocked out

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone sits inside their home, so one piece goes inside the other
something knocked out is removed, here the card-suit abbreviation

parts.note: the French are a European nation
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: rearranged means put into a different order

explanation.surface: A frantic scene: a necktie redone by continental guests while a football team is beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts doubles as an Edinburgh football club, but here it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means wildly agitated and fast-paced, a near synonym for hectic.

clue.text: Players covering an area in game

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the players word encloses the next one

parts.note: the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Competitors cover a region of the field during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game, so it is a game.

clue.text: Opportunity in Germany? Enthusiastic comment about that

indicators.note: about means around, and that points back to the opening phrase, which goes inside

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A chance in Germany? Someone greets the news with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a short period when something is possible, as in a window of opportunity.

clue.text: Unidentified thing with energy quota cropping up again?

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A mystery object plus a share of power keeps reappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: an iteration is a repeat, the act of coming round again.
explanation.definitionFit: An iteration is a repetition of a process, so it is the business of something recurring.

clue.text: Lecturer welcoming the old senior member

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: An academic greets the venerable senior fellow of the college.
explanation.definitionFit: The doyen of a group is its most senior or respected member, its acknowledged elder.

clue.text: Had to accept upturns in less potent drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up runs it bottom to top

parts.note: you faced what you had to accept

explanation.surface: Someone had to settle for a weaker drink as things looked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is coffee with the caffeine removed, so it is less potent than ordinary coffee.

clue.text: Detective, glum, missing second round

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter drops out

parts.note: the second round letter in the word, a ring shape

explanation.surface: A gloomy investigator skips the next round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for glum has two round letters; it is the second that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is the famous Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series.

clue.text: Very pleasant composer welcoming one into company

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the composer holds the other letters
one letter goes into the other piece, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A delightful composer makes a newcomer at home in the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicious can mean delightful in general, not just tasty, so very pleasant fits.

clue.text: Wise figure picking up some philosophical work

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up lifts the letters so they read upwards
some means a portion, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sage figure collecting a piece of philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is the traditional emblem of wisdom, linked to Athena.

clue.text: French coming in to reinvigorate Scottish town

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the other word, ending up inside it

parts.note: to renew is to refresh or revive

explanation.surface: French visitors arrive to bring new life to a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Renfrew is a town west of Glasgow, historic county town of Renfrewshire.

clue.text: Spanish composer, excellent, quite the foremost in Andalusia

parts.note: all, as in all alone meaning quite alone

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: A superb Spanish composer, quite the best in Andalusia.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel de Falla was the Spanish composer of The Three-Cornered Hat, born in Cádiz in Andalusia.
